description: The Carol M. Highsmith Archive features photographs documenting primarily the United States through more than 70,000 photos. The collection, which spans from 1980 to the present, includes landmark buildings, architectural renovation projects, landscapes and cityscapes, people and cultural events in a combined portrait of daily life. The archive is expected to grow to more than 100,000 photographs.

description: Potter Richard "Dick" Lehman discusses his career, including his shift from religious work to pottery; learning to run a business; establishing a building where many craftspeople/ artists had retail shops; getting advice from other potters; supporting his employees at the pottery and how they contributed; planning a sabbatical while self-employed; responding to customers' needs; the many entities that contribute to the local arts community; and shifting to working alone in his new studio.

description: Dick Davis grew up interested in the outdoors, but joined the Navy after high school instead of going to college. After the Vietnam War, Davis, influenced by the era's increased interest in environmentalism, went back to school and received the necessary education to eventually secure a summer interpreter position, and then a full-time naturalist position. In this interview, Dick recalls learning how to interpret and plan programming, explains the formation of the Indiana state parks system and talks about maintaining facilities, working with mentors, and training new employees.

description: Now working at Indiana Caverns, a commercial property, Carol Groves began her interpretive career at Patoka Lake. In this interview, she details the many differences between private and public sector work, her process of planning programming and exhibits, and the camaraderie she shared with her co-workers. She also discusses the political system that was in place when she was hired, as well as the negative associations that some local families still have with the property because of unfair land acquisition practices.
